strings.screen.mass.monstrance.intro: The monstrance — from the Latin monstrare, “to show” — is a sacred vessel that holds the consecrated Host up for the faithful to see and adore. It is used for Eucharistic Adoration, Benediction and processions. The monstrance itself is not worshipped; it is a sacred vessel that points us to Jesus, truly present in the Eucharist.
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.cross.name: Cross
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.cross.desc: At the very top, the sign of our salvation in Christ.
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.sunburst.name: Sunburst
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.sunburst.desc: The rays of glory that represent the radiance of Christ, the “Sun of Justice.”
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.ostensorium.name: Ostensorium
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.ostensorium.desc: The central circular opening, or window, that displays the Eucharist for adoration.
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.glass_front.name: Glass Door (Front)
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.glass_front.desc: Protects the Eucharist while allowing it to be seen.
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.lunula.name: Lunula
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.lunula.desc: The crescent holder that keeps the host in place; its shape resembles the moon, a symbol of Our Lady.
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.host.name: The Host
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.host.desc: The Blessed Sacrament — the Body, Blood, Soul and Divinity of Jesus Christ.
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.glass_back.name: Glass Door (Back)
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.glass_back.desc: Seals and protects the Eucharist from the rear.
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.back_cover.name: Back Cover
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.back_cover.desc: Provides protection and reverence for the Eucharist.
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.node.name: Node
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.node.desc: The knop on the stem, worked with wheat and vine — the Bread of Life and the True Vine.
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.shaft.name: Shaft
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.shaft.desc: The stem that connects the base to the sunburst — our journey in faith, lifting our hearts to Christ.
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.base.name: Base
strings.screen.mass.monstrance.base.desc: Provides stability and honours the sacred presence of Jesus.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.intro: The thurible is a sacred vessel used to burn incense. The rising smoke is a sign of our prayers ascending to God — “Let my prayer be counted as incense before you” (Psalm 141:2). It is used at the Entrance, the Gospel, the Preparation of the Gifts, the Eucharistic Prayer and Benediction.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.types.title: Types of thuribles and censers
strings.screen.mass.thurible.type.single_chain.d: A compact censer suspended from one chain, a form found in some Eastern Christian traditions.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.type.three_chain.de: A censer suspended by three chains, used in several Christian liturgical traditions and balanced for ceremonial swinging.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.type.four_chain.des: A censer suspended by four chains, especially associated with Eastern Christian use.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.type.four_chain_bel: A four-chain censer fitted with small bells that sound as it is swung, common in Eastern Christian worship.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.type.roman.name: Roman Catholic Thurible
strings.screen.mass.thurible.type.roman.desc: The familiar Western Catholic thurible: a perforated metal bowl and lid suspended from chains, used at Mass, processions, Benediction and other solemn rites.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.type.stationary.des: A censer made to remain in one place rather than being carried and swung, used to burn incense in particular liturgical settings.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.type.ceremonial.des: An unusually large and richly worked censer used for major celebrations or designed for a particular church.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.type.botafumeiro.de: The monumental swinging censer of Santiago de Compostela Cathedral, carried through the transept on a rope system during certain major celebrations.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.finial.name: Finial (Cross)
strings.screen.mass.thurible.finial.desc: The cross on top, a reminder that our prayers are offered in the name of Christ.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.lid.name: Lid (Cover)
strings.screen.mass.thurible.lid.desc: The perforated cover that lets the smoke rise, symbolising prayers ascending to heaven.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.charcoal.name: Charcoal Plate
strings.screen.mass.thurible.charcoal.desc: Holds the burning charcoal on which the incense is placed.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.bowl.name: Censer Bowl
strings.screen.mass.thurible.bowl.desc: The cup that holds the charcoal and incense — the heart of the thurible.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.chains.name: Chains
strings.screen.mass.thurible.chains.desc: Usually three, for faith, hope and love; they balance the thurible as it is swung.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.ring.name: Suspension Ring
strings.screen.mass.thurible.ring.desc: The ring at the top from which the chains hang.
strings.screen.mass.thurible.handle.name: Handle
strings.screen.mass.thurible.handle.desc: Used by the thurifer to raise the lid and swing the thurible during the liturgy.
strings.screen.mass.vessels.intro: Because they hold the Eucharist, the vessels of the altar are made of precious metal (or lined with it), blessed for sacred use, and handled only with reverence.
strings.screen.mass.vessels.chalice.name: Chalice
strings.screen.mass.vessels.chalice.desc: The cup that holds the wine which becomes the Blood of Christ.
strings.screen.mass.vessels.paten.name: Paten
strings.screen.mass.vessels.paten.desc: The small plate that holds the priest's host.
strings.screen.mass.vessels.ciborium.name: Ciborium
strings.screen.mass.vessels.ciborium.desc: The covered cup that holds the hosts for the Communion of the faithful and reserves them in the tabernacle.
strings.screen.mass.vessels.cruets.name: Cruets
strings.screen.mass.vessels.cruets.desc: The small jugs of wine and water brought to the altar at the Preparation of the Gifts.
strings.screen.mass.vessels.pyx.name: Pyx
strings.screen.mass.vessels.pyx.desc: The small round case used to carry Communion to the sick.
strings.screen.mass.vessels.luna.name: Luna
strings.screen.mass.vessels.luna.desc: The crescent clip that holds the Host upright in the monstrance for adoration.
strings.screen.mass.postures.intro: At Mass the whole body prays. The faithful stand, sit and kneel together at set moments — a shared language of reverence that expresses one faith in one body.
strings.screen.mass.postures.responses: Throughout the Mass the people answer the priest. To “The Lord be with you” they reply “And with your spirit”; the readings close with “Thanks be to God” and “Praise to you, Lord Jesus Christ”; and to the great prayers the assembly seals its assent with “Amen.”
strings.screen.mass.postures.stand.name: Standing
strings.screen.mass.postures.stand.desc: For prayer and to honour the Gospel — the posture of the risen and the attentive.
strings.screen.mass.postures.sit.name: Sitting
strings.screen.mass.postures.sit.desc: For the readings before the Gospel and the homily — the posture of listening.
strings.screen.mass.postures.kneel.name: Kneeling
strings.screen.mass.postures.kneel.desc: During the Eucharistic Prayer and before Communion — the posture of adoration and humility.
strings.screen.mass.postures.genuflect.name: Genuflection
strings.screen.mass.postures.genuflect.desc: Bending the right knee toward the tabernacle, adoring Christ present in the Eucharist.
strings.screen.mass.postures.bow.name: Bowing
strings.screen.mass.postures.bow.desc: A bow of the head at the holy names, and a deeper bow before receiving Communion.
strings.screen.mass.postures.sign.name: The Sign of the Cross
strings.screen.mass.postures.sign.desc: Made at the beginning and end, marking the whole prayer as Christ's.
strings.screen.mass.altar.intro: The altar is the heart of the church. It is at once the table of the Lord's Supper and the altar of sacrifice, where the offering of Calvary is made present — and so it stands for Christ himself.
strings.screen.mass.altar.markings: When a new altar is dedicated, the bishop anoints it with sacred chrism and incenses it. Five crosses are carved or marked into it — one at each corner and one in the centre — recalling the five wounds of Christ. In many altars the relics of a saint, often a martyr, are sealed within or beneath the altar stone, an ancient link to the tombs on which the early Church offered Mass.
strings.screen.mass.altar.kiss_body: The priest kisses the altar because it stands for Christ, the cornerstone. At a solemn Mass it is also honoured with incense — the same reverence shown to the Gospel and to the gifts.
strings.screen.mass.altar.crucifix.name: The Crucifix
strings.screen.mass.altar.crucifix.desc: A cross bearing the figure of the crucified Christ stands on or near the altar, in view of the assembly.
strings.screen.mass.altar.candles.name: Candles
strings.screen.mass.altar.candles.desc: At least two lit candles (up to six, or seven for a bishop) — a sign of reverence and festivity.
strings.screen.mass.altar.flowers.name: Flowers
strings.screen.mass.altar.flowers.desc: May adorn the altar in moderation according to the season; never during Lent, and sparingly in Advent.
strings.screen.mass.altar.frontal.name: The Frontal
strings.screen.mass.altar.frontal.desc: An antependium may hang before the altar in the colour of the day.
strings.screen.mass.altar.altarcloth.name: Altar Cloth
strings.screen.mass.altar.altarcloth.desc: The white “fair linen” that covers the altar table; earlier custom used three cloths together.
strings.screen.mass.altar.corporal.name: The Corporal
strings.screen.mass.altar.corporal.desc: A square cloth unfolded at the centre of the altar, on which the chalice and paten rest so no fragment of the Host is lost.
strings.screen.mass.altar.purificator.name: The Purificator
strings.screen.mass.altar.purificator.desc: A small folded cloth used to wipe the chalice and the priest's fingers.
strings.screen.mass.altar.pall.name: The Pall
strings.screen.mass.altar.pall.desc: A stiff linen-covered square laid over the chalice to keep anything from falling into it.
strings.screen.mass.procession.thurifer.title: Thurible Bearer
strings.screen.mass.procession.thurifer.descript: The thurible bearer leads the procession with burning incense — a sign of our prayers rising up to God, and a mark of honour for the sacred things that follow.
strings.screen.mass.procession.crossbearer.title: Cross Bearer
strings.screen.mass.procession.crossbearer.descr: The processional cross leads the ministers forward, the sign of Christ who goes before us. All who follow walk behind the Cross toward the altar.
strings.screen.mass.procession.candlebearer.desc: Acolytes carry lit candles on either side of the cross — Christ, the Light of the World, whose light the Church carries into the assembly.
strings.screen.mass.procession.bellringer.title: Bell Ringer
strings.screen.mass.procession.bellringer.descri: A bell may be rung to announce the procession and to call the faithful to worship, gathering the whole assembly into one attentive prayer.
strings.screen.mass.procession.bookbearer.title: Book Bearer
strings.screen.mass.procession.bookbearer.descri: The Book of the Gospels is carried aloft — the Word of God proclaimed in the Mass. It is set upon the altar until the moment of the Gospel.
strings.screen.mass.procession.priest.title: The Priest
strings.screen.mass.procession.priest.descriptio: The priest follows last as the one who presides. He represents Christ himself, the Head of the Church, and it is he who will offer the sacrifice at the altar.
strings.screen.sacraments.baptism.title: Baptism
strings.screen.sacraments.baptism.sign: Immersion in water, or the pouring of water, with the words: “I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.”
strings.screen.sacraments.baptism.grace: Washes away original and personal sin, makes us children of God and members of the Church, and marks the soul forever.
strings.screen.sacraments.baptism.description: Baptism is the gateway to the whole sacramental life. Through water and the word a person dies to sin and is reborn as a child of God, receives the Holy Spirit, and is joined to the Body of Christ. It can be received only once, for its mark on the soul is permanent.
strings.screen.sacraments.eucharist.title: The Eucharist
strings.screen.sacraments.eucharist.sign: Bread and wine which, through the priest's words of consecration, become the Body and Blood of Christ.
strings.screen.sacraments.eucharist.grace: Unites us most intimately to Christ, forgives venial sin, and is the source and summit of the Christian life.
strings.screen.sacraments.eucharist.description: The Eucharist is the true Body and Blood, soul and divinity of Jesus Christ under the appearances of bread and wine. Instituted at the Last Supper, it is offered in every Mass and received in Holy Communion. The Church calls it the source and summit of the whole Christian life.
strings.screen.sacraments.confirmation.title: Confirmation
strings.screen.sacraments.confirmation.sign: Anointing of the forehead with sacred chrism, with the laying on of hands and the words: “Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit.”
strings.screen.sacraments.confirmation.grace: Completes baptismal grace and strengthens the Christian with the sevenfold gift of the Holy Spirit to witness to the faith.
strings.screen.sacraments.confirmation.descripti: Confirmation perfects what Baptism began. The bishop or priest anoints the confirmand with chrism, sealing them with the Holy Spirit as the apostles were sealed at Pentecost. It deepens the bond with the Church and gives strength to profess and defend the faith in word and deed.
strings.screen.sacraments.penance.title: Penance & Reconciliation
strings.screen.sacraments.penance.sign: The penitent's contrition and confession of sins, and the words of absolution spoken by the priest.
strings.screen.sacraments.penance.grace: Reconciles the sinner with God and the Church, forgiving sins committed after Baptism and restoring grace.
strings.screen.sacraments.penance.description: In this sacrament of healing a person confesses their sins to a priest, who — acting in the person of Christ — grants God's forgiveness through absolution. It restores the friendship with God lost through sin and brings peace of conscience. Its acts are contrition, confession, and satisfaction.
strings.screen.sacraments.matrimony.group: Sacrament at the Service of Communion
strings.screen.sacraments.matrimony.title: Matrimony
strings.screen.sacraments.matrimony.sign: The consent of a baptized man and woman freely exchanged before the Church.
strings.screen.sacraments.matrimony.grace: Establishes a lifelong bond and gives the couple grace to love as Christ loves, and to welcome and raise children.
strings.screen.sacraments.matrimony.description: In Matrimony a baptized man and woman give themselves to each other in a covenant of love for life. Their consent, exchanged before God and the Church, makes them ministers of the sacrament to one another. Christ strengthens their union to be faithful, fruitful, and a living sign of his love for the Church.
strings.screen.sacraments.holy_orders.group: Sacrament at the Service of Communion
strings.screen.sacraments.holy_orders.title: Holy Orders
strings.screen.sacraments.holy_orders.sign: The laying on of the bishop's hands and the solemn prayer of consecration.
strings.screen.sacraments.holy_orders.grace: Configures the man to Christ the Head and Shepherd, empowering him to serve as deacon, priest or bishop.
strings.screen.sacraments.holy_orders.descriptio: Through Holy Orders, chosen men are ordained to serve the Church in the person of Christ. Its three degrees are deacon, priest and bishop. Priests preach, forgive sins and offer the Eucharist; bishops hold the fullness of the sacrament and continue the mission of the apostles. Like Baptism, it marks the soul permanently.
Anointing of the forehead and hands with blessed oil, with the Church's prayer for the sick person.
Unites the sick to Christ's Passion, gives strength, peace and courage, forgives sins, and may restore health.

The Anointing of the Sick is for those who begin to be in danger from illness or old age. The priest anoints them with holy oil, commending them to the suffering and risen Lord. It brings spiritual strength, the forgiveness of sins, and — if God wills — bodily healing. It is not only for the dying.
